source_text: Περὶ ἀναστάσεως πρὸς Σαδδουκαίους. «Πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ Θεοῦ· ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἀναστάσει οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίζονται.» Ἀλληγορητέον ὡς παρὰ τῷ Ἀποστόλῳ περὶ παιδίσκης καὶ ἐλευθέρας· οἱ σωματικῶς τὰ περὶ γάμων ἐκλαμβάνοντες πλανῶνται ὥσπερ οἱ μετὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν βρώματα σωματικὰ προσδοκῶντες. «Θεὸς οὐκ ἔστιν νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων· πάντες γὰρ αὐτῷ ζῶσιν.» Δόξα Χριστῷ. Ἀμήν.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning resurrection toward Sadducees. «You-err not knowing the writings nor the power of God; for in the resurrection neither they-marry nor are-married.» It-is-to-be-allegorized as with the Apostle concerning slave-girl and free-woman; those bodily the things about marriages taking err just-as those after the resurrection foods bodily expecting. «God is-not of-dead but of-living; for all to-him live.» Glory to Christ. Amen.
pass_b_english: On the resurrection against the Sadducees. [[You are wrong, not knowing the Scriptures or the power of God; for in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage >> Bible:Matthew 22:29-30]]. Read it allegorically, as Paul does the slave woman and the free. Those who take marriage texts bodily err like those expecting bodily foods after the rising. [[God is not of the dead but of the living; for all live to him >> Bible:Luke 20:38]]. Glory to Christ. Amen.
notes: Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
